parsed.explanation: Combined national-Oklahoma regime imposes tier-1 universal exposures: birth-sex passport/facility rules, entry refusal for document doubt with possible fraud ineligibility, K-12 and state-facility bans, birth-sex custody with documented conversion/hormone-removal and immigration-custody abuse. No execution or routine long imprisonment for presence, and courts have enjoined some orders with live challenges, so above 0.15-0.25 anchors, but operative birth-sex facilities/custody and entry screening keep it below 0.35-0.45.

entry_documents.exposure: National X-marker issuance ended; existing X valid to expiry. 2025 cable: document discrepancy or reasonable doubt on sex requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent fraud ineligibility. Passports reported confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; ACLU suit and court challenges pending; several executive orders blocked/enjoined. Fraud ground requires four elements and is not automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport M/F mismatch can trigger secondary screening, refusal, and fraud inquiry; state birth-certificate bans do not govern foreign passport but reinforce birth-sex document practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution. Immigration custody reports: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse. Bathroom trespass case: handcuffed, 24h men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No documented visitor-specific habeas, consular-access or custody-placement remedy in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document/facility encounter can become arrest, then birth-sex ward/cell placement and hormone denial; trespass requires wilful entry plus refusal to depart when asked, not automatic arrest.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars government single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Oklahoma: 2022/2025 K-12 bans using birth certificate; 2023 order defines sex by birth for state bathrooms, shelters, incarceration. Four states make some use criminal; first capitol restroom arrest documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 26+ states plus capital district lack mapped bans, but Oklahoma is in ban group. Statutory exemptions for emergencies, chaperoning, out-of-order facilities; no Oklahoma-wide identity access documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal, state-owned, school and private-setting rules stack; a visitor cannot avoid birth-sex facilities in schools/government buildings and faces trespass after refusal to leave.

care_services.exposure: Oklahoma SB904 (May 2026) bars public funds, Medicaid and state facilities for gender-affirming surgeries, blockers and hormones for minors and adults; employee violations are misdemeanours. National orders/proposed rules target under-18 care.
care_services.protection: Private facilities with private insurance/out-of-pocket remain available; exemptions for counselling, mental-health meds, intersex, complications and emergency life/limb care.
care_services.interaction: Adult visitor may obtain private care but not public-system continuity; hospital ward placement by document/birth sex remains a separate exposure if injured.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National binary definition, removal of gender-identity policies, trans-athlete entry ban, counterterrorism language prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups and cash-reward memo using 'radical gender ideology'. Oklahoma law defines women/girls by reproductive biology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 Supreme Court employment ruling and 2009 national hate-crime statute cover gender identity federally; several orders enjoined; courts are actively hearing challenges.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases discretion at borders, schools and facilities, while functioning courts provide partial, non-immediate recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor must use birth-certificate facilities at K-12, sports barred by birth sex, gender-affirming care banned and publicly funded care barred; national order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition. Guardian may face school/facility and care denial.
minors_guardians.protection: Private care and emergency care exemptions documented; no documented visitor/minor school-enrolment or guardian protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling minor is exposed at school, sports, bathrooms and clinics; parent/guardian cannot cure birth-sex document rules and may be investigated if seeking affirming care through public systems.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No visitor-specific violence documented. Resident signals: 2018 death threats including mutilation/castration after trans student outing; 2024 Nex Benedict death shortly after bathroom beating. Oklahoma hate-crime law does not cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute allows federal prosecution; one city bans discrimination in employment/housing/public accommodations, three others only city employment.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State-level non-coverage leaves visitors reliant on federal prosecution; police response to visitor assault not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Oklahoma has no state gender-identity discrimination protection; at-will employment; HB1225 birth-certificate bill status, licence-marker status, and July 2026 traveller grade not documented. Entry/custody remedies for visitors not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU passport suit, challenges to executive orders, legal-aid FAQ, injunctions on some orders. National courts allowed passport restriction to take effect in Nov 2025, showing limits.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation may change rules mid-travel or after departure; documented injunctions do not pre-empt operative entry, facility or custody rules shown in force.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar or slightly higher: both impose birth-sex prison/facility placement with assault risk and slow remedies. This case adds national entry-refusal/fraud risk and documented hormone-removal custody, but no routine imprisonment for presentation, so not materially below 0.25.

Lower: 0.35-A is exclusion/humiliation without imprisonment. Here universal birth-sex facilities, criminal trespass after refusal, birth-sex custody abuse and potential lifetime entry ineligibility are more severe, despite live court challenges.

Higher: 0.15-A has routine arrest, months pretrial, beatings, illusory appeals and capital provision. Here arrest is documented but trespass-specific, imprisonment not routine, courts actively enjoin some measures, and no credible execution pathway is documented.

Much lower: 0.55-C is ward placement by marker with ethics/advocate remedies and no detention pathway. Here facility bans are statutory, criminalised in some circumstances, entry can be refused, and custody abuse is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Operative interaction is document mismatch or facility use -> questioning/refusal, possible trespass arrest, birth-sex ward/cell and hormone interruption; for minors, school/sports/care bans compound this. Courts, existing X validity, private care and federal hate-crime law are real but partial and slow, not shown to prevent the initial universal exposure. That combination places the regime between 0.25 birth-sex custody anchors and 0.35 exclusion-only anchors.
